questions.correct_answer: It is non-superimposable on its mirror image
questions.explanation: A chiral molecule cannot be superimposed on its mirror image, usually because it has a stereocenter with four different groups. Molecules with an internal plane of symmetry are achiral, so that option is a common mistake.
options: It is non-superimposable on its mirror image
It contains at least one double bond
It has an internal plane of symmetry
It causes plane-polarized light to rotate by exactly 0 degrees
questions.question: Which property defines a molecule as chiral?

questions.correct_answer: Using a stronger nucleophile such as iodide in acetone
questions.explanation: SN2 is bimolecular, so its rate depends on the nucleophile's strength, and polar aprotic solvents like acetone leave the nucleophile unsolvated and more reactive. Tertiary substrates and polar protic solvents favor SN1 or slow SN2, and weak leaving groups slow both pathways.
options: Switching to a polar protic solvent such as methanol
Using a stronger nucleophile such as iodide in acetone
Changing the substrate to a tertiary alkyl halide
Making the leaving group a weaker leaving group
questions.question: Which change would most increase the rate of an SN2 reaction of 1-bromobutane with a nucleophile?

questions.correct_answer: They differ only in how electrons are arranged, while the positions of the atoms stay the same
questions.explanation: Resonance structures are different Lewis depictions of one molecule with the same atomic connectivity and differing only in electron placement. The real molecule is a weighted average (resonance hybrid), not a structure that flips between forms, and the pi bond count can differ between contributors.
options: They differ only in how electrons are arranged, while the positions of the atoms stay the same
They are different isomers that interconvert rapidly
The real molecule alternates between the resonance forms over time
All resonance structures must contain the same number of pi bonds
questions.question: Which statement about resonance structures is correct?
